transcript.content:
hey, i'm berry.

tell me your dream, however it comes back to you.
It looked like a comic book. Thick black lines, flat colours.

like the whole world was drawn that way.

what was happening?
I was standing on this tiny train station platform in the middle of a desert.

a train platform in the middle of a desert, all by itself.

who else was there, if anyone?
There was this old man in a white suit sitting on the bench. And a camel standing right next to him, totally calm.

a camel just standing next to him like it's the most normal thing.

was the old man doing anything?
He told me the train was late. Said it like it always is.

like nobody was surprised, least of all him.

then what?
I looked at the clock on the pole and it was melting. Dripping down like wax.

the whole thing was coming apart in the heat.

how did that feel, seeing the clock melt?
Weirdly calm? I just stared at it. Everything looked so flat, even the shadows were hard black shapes.

calm, even with the whole world looking like that.

what stayed with you most after you woke up?
The old man and the camel walking off into the desert. Just getting smaller and smaller while I stayed on the platform.

so you watched them go, and you stayed put.

was the old man someone you knew, or a stranger?
Stranger. Never seen him before.

and it didn't feel strange, him walking off like that.

what came right before that, when he started leaving?
I heard a train whistle far away. But no train ever came. Then he just got up and the camel followed him.

all that waiting, and still no train.

how did it sound, that whistle?
Far off. Like it was coming from somewhere that wasn't really there.

like the sound belonged to somewhere else.

did you follow them, or stay?
Stayed. Just stood there watching until they were tiny.

and no train ever showed.

was there anything you wanted to hold onto from it, some object or thing that mattered?
The clock, maybe. The way it drooped, like it gave up on being a clock.

that image's gonna stick, the clock that couldn't hold its own shape.

what did the sky look like in that desert?
Bright, like the sun was straight overhead. Made every shadow a hard black shape.

so bright it flattened everything out.

were there colours you remember most?
Just flat ones, like from a comic book. Nothing blended. I don't remember exact colours.

so you were standing on a tiny train station platform in the middle of a desert, and the whole world looked like a comic book, thick black lines and flat colours, with the sun so bright overhead every shadow was a hard black shape. an old man in a white suit sat on a bench, a calm camel right next to him. he told you the train was late, like it always is. you looked at the clock on the pole and it was melting, dripping down like wax, and you felt weirdly calm, just staring. then you heard a train whistle far away, like from somewhere that wasn't really there, but no train ever came. the old man got up, the camel followed, and they walked off into the desert getting smaller and smaller while you stayed on the platform. the clock stuck with you, the way it drooped like it gave up on being a clock.

did i get that right, or did i miss anything?
You got it right. That's exactly how it was.

i can see it.

would you like to see it drawn?
Yes, I would.

there are a few ways it could be drawn.

it could be a classic comic book: crisp and unreal, like a story you could hold. or a retro pop-art screenprint: loud and iconic, like a symbol burned into memory. or a stark ink drawing with one colour: sharp and intense, like a moment cut into the page. or how it actually looked: like standing in that impossible sunshine, every shadow a hole cut out of the world. which feels closest, or would you describe your own?
How it actually looked. That impossible sunshine and hard black shadows.

let's start with the desert platform.

i picture a tiny train station platform standing alone in a vast desert, tracks beside it. there's a bench, a pole with a clock, endless flat sand, distant horizon. bright sunlight from directly overhead, so shadows are hard black shapes. those are my guesses.

does any of that feel different, or would you leave it to me?
That sounds right. Leave it to you.

okay, i'll keep it that way.

what did the old man look like, up close?
Don't remember his face. Just the white suit. And how calm he was.

that's enough, white suit and that calmness it is. i'm sketching the desert platform, the old man, the camel, and the melting clock now, it'll appear on the right, just those for now.

as you are, if you want to say a little about yourself, or however i imagine you?
I don't have much to say about myself. Imagine me how you want.

then i'll imagine you there, small under that bare sun.

i'm sketching you in now. everything will come together on the right in the next minute or two, and you can tell me if anything looks off once it appears.
It all looks right. The melting clock especially.

that melting clock was worth getting right.

is there anything you'd change, or does it feel done?
It feels done. Nothing to change.

good, done feels right.

i'll draw the moments of the dream in order now, each carrying on from the ones before it, and they'll appear on the right as they're ready.
Okay. I'll wait for the rest.

two of the seven moments are on the right now, the rest are still on their way.

do those first two look the way you remember?
I don't know which two you mean, but if it's the platform and the old man with the camel, those are right.

the two on the right are the moment you're standing on the tiny platform, the old man and the camel there, and then you looking at the clock on the pole.

the other five are still being drawn.
That fits, especially me just staring at the clock. Four now, still waiting on the rest.

the melting clock was a good one to get. four are up now, the old man saying the train is late, and him getting up, the camel following. once these look right, i'll draw the rest.

do they look the way you saw them?
Five now. They all fit what I remember. The old man getting up is right, camel just following like it was nothing.

five down, two still to come. the camel just following like it was nothing, that's the part you'd remember.

i'll draw the last two now, they carry on from the clock and the shadows.
Six. It's still matching. Just the last one left.

six on the right now, the old man and the camel tiny shapes in the distance, one more still to come.

do those tiny shapes look the way you remember?
Now seven. The tiny shapes are right. That's exactly the view from the platform.

all seven are up, and you're happy with those tiny shapes.

does the whole thing look the way you remember?
Yes, the whole thing looks right. Even the flat colours and the hard shadows.

that's lovely to hear. the flat colours and hard shadows came through just right.

thank you for sharing this dream with me, you can look through it all there on the right.
